text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds slightly firm after retreating from day's high of 98.28. Market seen continuing to consolidate, awaiting Ifo August business climate index due Thursday, August M3. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.08, down 0.05 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts slithered lower in afternoon trade, hit by a wobble in U.S. Treasuries and December futures ended down 13/32. Traders said the UK monetary meeting on Monday and U.S. FOMC on Tuesday will keep investors sidelined. They expect no quick bounce back. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-14/32, down 13/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bonds end near lows as Bunds slip late in session. Budget had little effect as it had been leaked, though profit taking on franc hit PIBOR. 10-yr spread widens slightly. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.86 down 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt instruments ended a negative session down but off day's lows, sentiment depressed by a corruption probe involving the head of Italy state railways. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 117.69 down 0.22 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries in plus column after US trade gap widens 42.6 pct to $11.68 bln. Economists seen revising down Q3 GDP estimates slightly in wake of numbers. Earlier, "top Fed source" plays down importance of last week's tepid inflation/retail sales data in Fed thinking.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-03/32, down 01/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.01 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo at the day's high on Wednesday, recovering early losses which stemmed partly from corrective selling to their steep advance on Tuesday. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.36, up 0.43 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The launch of two asset-backed Eurobonds on Wednesday gave a further boost to this nascent European market, dealers said. The first Finnish markka-denominated international asset-backed deal was issued by Fennica. The three-tranche deal consisted of fixed- and floating-rate class A notes. An official at joint lead manager ING Barings said the deal represented another step in the development of the European asset-backed sector. "It is the first such deal syndicated internationally, and the FRN is the first markka floater too," the official said.
